sourcedFrom: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A (not printed)
cleanIntro: The 590DA1 is a Model 590 pump with a double-action trigger: cycling the action only partly cocks the hammer, and the long trigger pull finishes the job. It comes apart like a 590 - the barrel is held by the magazine cap on the end of the tube, not a takedown screw. The safety is the button on the top rear of the receiver: fully rearward, over the red dot, is SAFE. The action lock lever is on the left of the trigger housing, just behind the trigger guard. Its barrels and trigger housings do not interchange with the 500, the 835 or non-DA1 receivers.

steps.title: Safety button fully rearward - SAFE
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, fingers off the trigger. Slide the safety button on the top rear of the receiver fully rearward into its detent, over the red dot.
steps.prose: Rearward is SAFE. The red dot only shows the direction; Mossberg says not to read it as an indicator that the safety is on.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward (Fig. 2) to the "ON" (SAFE) position.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Lock lever down, forearm back slowly - chambered shell out by hand
steps.action: Press the action lock lever on the left side of the trigger housing and draw the forearm rearward slowly until the chambered shell is fully out and visible in the ejection port. Lift it out by hand.
steps.prose: Slowly, so the shell stops in the port where you can take it instead of being thrown.
steps.quote: slowly, until the live shotshell is completely withdrawn and visible in the ejection port. Remove shotshell by hand.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Keep pulling - next shell onto the elevator, port down to drop it
steps.action: Keep drawing the forearm back until the next shell drops onto the elevator, then turn the shotgun so the ejection port faces down and the shell falls out.
steps.prose: The ejection port is on the right side. Catch the shell as it drops.
steps.quote: Continue pulling the forearm rearward to release the next shotshell onto the elevator.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Forearm forward, gun over, right thumb on the cartridge stop
steps.action: Push the forearm completely forward so the bolt closes on an empty chamber. Turn the gun over, trigger guard up, still pointed somewhere safe. Put your right thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver and press the cartridge stop on the right side; the shells come out one at a time. Repeat until the magazine tube is empty.
steps.prose: One shell per press. Count them against what you loaded.
steps.quote: Insert your right thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver and depress the cartridge stop on the right side to release shotshells one at a time (Fig. 9). Repeat until all shotshells are removed from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Action open, look again at chamber, elevator and tube
steps.action: Press the action lock lever and pull the forearm completely rearward. Look into the chamber, at the elevator and into the magazine tube once more. Leave the action open and the safety fully rearward.
steps.prose: The elevator is where a shell hides after a partial unload. Look at it; do not assume.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever and pull the forearm completely rearward. Visually inspect chamber, elevator and magazine tube again to insure that no shotshells remain in the shotgun.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — UNLOADING, p.7
steps.warn: Leave the action in the open, rearward position and the safety button fully rearward in the "ON" (SAFE) position.

steps.title: Safety SAFE, chamber, elevator and magazine checked
steps.action: With the safety button fully rearward, check the chamber, the elevator and the magazine once more before anything comes off. Put on eye protection.
steps.prose: Mossberg asks for eye protection for disassembly and cleaning both.
steps.quote: Position the safety button fully rearward in the "ON" (SAFE) position and check chamber, elevator and magazine to be certain gun is unloaded.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY / BARREL REMOVAL, p.7

steps.title: Lock lever down, forearm fully rearward
steps.action: Press the action lock lever and slide the forearm all the way back to open the action.
steps.prose: The lever is on the left side of the trigger housing, just behind the trigger guard.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever (Fig. 3) and open the action by sliding the forearm fully rearward.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY / BARREL REMOVAL, p.7

steps.title: Forearm forward until the bolt face sits mid-port
steps.action: Move the forearm slowly forward from fully rearward and stop when the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port.
steps.prose: That is the position the barrel comes off in - not fully open and not closed.
steps.quote: Move the forearm slowly forward from the fully rearward position until the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port (Fig. 7).
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY / BARREL REMOVAL, p.7

steps.title: Magazine cap off - counter-clockwise
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap at the front end of the magazine tube by turning it counter-clockwise until it comes off.
steps.prose: On this gun the cap is what holds the barrel on. The magazine spring stays in the tube behind its retainer.
steps.quote: Unscrew the magazine cap by turning it counterclockwise
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — BARREL ASSEMBLY, p.4

steps.title: Barrel out with a gentle back-and-forth twist
steps.action: Work the barrel out of the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotation while pulling it forward, the takedown mount ring sliding off the magazine tube.
steps.prose: Gentle is the book's word. With the barrel off, leave the action and trigger alone.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotational movement while pulling the barrel out of the receiver assembly.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY / BARREL REMOVAL, p.8
steps.warn: Never close the action or pull trigger while barrel is removed as damage could result to the firearm.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrel is off. For normal use that is all this gun needs: bore, chamber, barrel extension and the exposed metal can all be cleaned now.
steps.prose: Mossberg's own field disassembly carries on into the trigger housing, bolt, bolt slide and elevator. That work is in Deep Clean, step by step from the book.
steps.quote: Normal use requires only that the mechanisms be free of excessive shooting residue.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.10

steps.title: Bore and chamber scrubbed, patched clean, a last oiled patch
steps.action: Scrub the bore and chamber with solvent, then push cleaning patches through until they come out clean. Finish with one lightly oiled patch, and clean any deposits out of the barrel extension.
steps.prose: Then look through the bore: no patch, no obstruction and no pooled oil before it goes back on.
steps.quote: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent and follow with cleaning patches until barrel is clean. A final pass with a lightly oiled patch will provide a protective coating. Clean and remove any deposits in the barrel extension
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.10

steps.title: Solvent on the metal, then a light coat of gun oil
steps.action: Clean all metal parts with gun solvent and give them a light coat of gun oil.
steps.prose: Light. Use only a lubricant made for firearms, and no abrasives on the finish.
steps.quote: All metal parts should be cleaned with gun solvent and lightly lubricated with gun oil.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.10

steps.title: Bolt and trigger housing cleaned whole - only if Deep Clean has them out
steps.action: If the bolt and trigger housing are out, clean each as one complete assembly with gun solvent and lubricate lightly with gun oil.
steps.prose: Both stay in one piece. Taking either apart is factory or gunsmith work.
steps.quote: The bolt and trigger housing assemblies are complex assemblies and should not be disassembled except by factory or qualified gunsmith. Clean as complete assemblies with gun solvent and lightly lubricate with gun oil
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — BOLT AND TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLIES, p.10

steps.title: Long storage: cleaned, oiled, barrel open, no fabric case
steps.action: If the gun is going away for a long time, clean and oil it thoroughly first. Do not plug the barrel, and do not store it in a fabric-lined case.
steps.prose: A fabric lining soaks the oil off the steel and leaves it bare.
steps.quote: If the gun is to be stored for a long period of time it should be thoroughly cleaned and oiled. Do not plug barrel or store in a fabric lined case that will absorb lubricant from the gun.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.10

deepSteps.title: Barrel off, gun on a clean surface, trigger guard up
deepSteps.action: With the gun unloaded, the safety fully rearward and the barrel already off, lay the shotgun on a clean surface with the trigger guard facing up.
deepSteps.prose: Look at how the parts sit inside the receiver before anything comes out - they go back in the same relationship.
deepSteps.quote: Position the shotgun on a clean surface with the trigger guard upward.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.8

deepSteps.title: Trigger housing pin out with a blunt punch, 3/16" or smaller
deepSteps.action: With a blunt object no larger than 3/16" (4.76 mm) across, push out the small trigger housing retainer pin in the side of the receiver, about 1/2" below the rear of the trigger guard.
deepSteps.prose: Blunt, and no bigger than the book says, so the hole is not marked or opened up.
deepSteps.quote: push out the small diameter trigger housing retainer pin located on the side of the receiver, approximately a 1/2" (12.7 mm) below the rear of the trigger guard (Fig. 8).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.8

deepSteps.title: Trigger housing out, rear first - and it stays whole
deepSteps.action: Lift the trigger housing out of the receiver, rear end up first.
deepSteps.prose: That is as far as the housing goes. A 590DA1 housing does not fit a non-DA1 receiver, so keep it with this gun.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the trigger housing assembly by lifting the rear portion upward first.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.8
deepSteps.warn: The trigger housing is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled. Disassembly should only be performed by the factory or a qualified gunsmith.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Do not drop the hammer with the housing out
deepSteps.action: Leave the trigger alone while the housing is out of the receiver. Letting the hammer fall can hurt you or damage the assembly.
deepSteps.prose: The hammer also has to be cocked for the housing to go back in.
deepSteps.quote: Do not pull the trigger and allow the hammer to fall when the trigger housing assembly is removed from the receiver. To do so may result in personal injury or damage to the assembly
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.8

deepSteps.title: Cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop out
deepSteps.action: Take the cartridge interrupter out of the ejection-port side of the receiver and the cartridge stop out of the opposite side. A light tap on the sides of the receiver may free them.
deepSteps.prose: From here on, note how the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars sit together.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the cartridge interrupter from the ejection port side and cartridge stop from the opposite side. (It may be necessary to tap the sides of the receiver lightly to release these parts)
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.9
deepSteps.warn: Pay special attention to the position of the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bar assembly during this portion of the disassembly, as the parts must be in the same relationship during reassembly.

deepSteps.title: Bolt three-quarters back, bolt slide lifted out at the clearance cuts
deepSteps.action: Move the forearm and action slide back until the bolt and bolt slide are three-quarters of the way rearward. When the bottom of the bolt slide lines up with the clearance cuts in the receiver sides, lift the bolt slide up and out.
deepSteps.prose: It only comes out at that one position. If it will not lift, move the forearm a little rather than forcing it.
deepSteps.quote: Move the forearm/action slide assembly rearward so that the bolt assembly and bolt slide are three quarters of the way rearward.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.9

deepSteps.title: Bolt forward out through the barrel opening
deepSteps.action: Slide the bolt assembly forward and out of the receiver through the barrel opening at the front.
deepSteps.prose: Forward, the way the barrel came out - not out of the ejection port.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly by sliding it forward and out of the receiver assembly through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.9

deepSteps.title: Elevator pivoted up, arms squeezed, out
deepSteps.action: Pivot the front of the elevator up out of the receiver, squeeze its two open-end arms together until they clear their holes, and take the elevator out.
deepSteps.prose: The safety button must still be fully rearward, or the elevator will not come out.
deepSteps.quote: Squeeze the two arms which form the open end of the elevator assembly together sufficiently to disengage and remove the elevator from the receiver
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.9
deepSteps.warn: The safety button located on the upper rear of the receiver must be fully rearward in the "ON" (SAFE) position to remove the elevator assembly

deepSteps.title: Forearm and action slide forward off the magazine tube
deepSteps.action: Slide the forearm and action slide assembly forward and off the magazine tube.
deepSteps.prose: That is the last part the book takes off.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the forearm/action slide assembly by sliding it forward and off the magazine tube.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.10

deepSteps.title: Stop here - the book's field disassembly is complete
deepSteps.action: Barrel, trigger housing, cartridge interrupter and stop, bolt slide, bolt, elevator and forearm are all out. Go no further.
deepSteps.prose: Anything beyond this point is for the factory or a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: The shotgun should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning or maintenance. Further disassembly should only be performed at the factory or by a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNERS MANUAL FOR MODEL 590DA1 PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN — Part No. 16406 Rev. A — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.10

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Bore and chamber scrubbed with solvent, then patched until clean
A final lightly oiled patch through the bore
Deposits cleaned out of the barrel extension
Barrel free of obstructions and excess lubricant before it goes back on
Never close the action or pull the trigger while the barrel is off

cleaning.name: METAL PARTS
tasks: All metal parts cleaned with gun solvent
A light coat of gun oil - lubricants made for firearms only
Do not use abrasives on the metal finish

cleaning.name: BOLT AND TRIGGER HOUSING
tasks: Only if Deep Clean has them out: each cleaned as one complete assembly in gun solvent
Do not disassemble the bolt or the trigger housing
Do not pull the trigger with the housing out of the receiver

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Before long storage: thoroughly cleaned and oiled
Do not store in a fabric-lined case

reassembly: Field strip only: slide the barrel's takedown mount ring over the magazine tube while guiding the barrel extension into the receiver, rocking the barrel gently back and forth as you push it home. Look through the ejection port: the barrel extension must rest firmly against its cut in the top of the receiver. Then thread the magazine cap on clockwise, by hand, until tight.

Deep Clean, receiver first: receiver on a clean surface with the trigger housing opening up, safety button fully rearward (SAFE). Slide the forearm assembly onto the magazine tube, guiding the action slide bars into the cuts in the front of the receiver.
Elevator: squeeze its arms together so the buttons on it drop into the 1/4" holes in the receiver, then pivot it until its forward part is even with the outside edge of the receiver cavity.

Bolt: rear end first, bolt lock downward toward the front inside top of the receiver, in through the barrel opening. Press the ejector (in the receiver wall opposite the ejection port) so the bolt slides fully rearward with the ejector in its slot in the bolt. Push the elevator down until it rests against the bolt.

Bolt slide: rear of the bolt even with the rear of the clearance cuts, the notch on each action bar even with the cuts in the receiver walls. Bolt slide slotted side up, notch to the rear; lower its front end first so its protrusion drops into the cut under the bolt lock and the action bar slots. Hold it down and pull the forearm forward - bolt and slide must move freely. If they do not, do not force it: take it apart and reassemble, watching how bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars relate.
Cartridge stop and cartridge interrupter onto the inside walls of the receiver, hooks facing inward toward the centre of the cavity.

Trigger housing: hammer cocked, and only a 590DA1 housing. Hold the cartridge stop and interrupter against the walls with one hand, fit the lugs at the housing's front corners into the receiver slots and ease the rear down - do not force it. If it will not seat, check that the housing's internal pins are flush and the stop and interrupter are positioned properly. Line up the pin hole and push the trigger housing pin in until flush with the receiver.
Barrel back on as in the field-strip line above, magazine cap hand-tight, then run the function check.
fncheck: Safety fully rearward (SAFE), muzzle somewhere safe, chamber, elevator and magazine tube checked empty. Hold the action lock lever down and open and close the action several times - it should move freely. Close the action and, safety still ON, pull the trigger fully rearward: the hammer must not fall. Take your finger off the trigger and move the safety forward to OFF: the hammer must not fall. Pull the trigger fully rearward: the hammer should fall. Open the action and put the safety back to ON. If the gun does not do exactly this at every step, Mossberg's instruction is not to use it and to contact O.F. Mossberg & Sons.
